sanskrit_verse:
साक्षिणः श्रावयेद् वादिप्रतिवादिसमीपगान् ।
ये पातककृतां लोका महापातकिनां तथा ॥७३॥
transliteration: sākṣiṇaḥ śrāvayed vādiprativādisamīpagān / ye pātakakṛtāṃ lokā mahāpātakināṃ tathā // YajñS_2.73
sph_interpretive_translation: Those witnesses who are present near the disputants in a trial shall declare the truth regarding persons who have committed sins, particularly those guilty of grave transgressions.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority resides in truthful witnessing as a dharma-duty
Causation arises from conscious presence during conflict resolution
Capacity-based responsibility includes the obligation to speak truth when positioned as witness
Restoration logic demands purification of falsehood through verified testimony
Consciousness alignment requires that testimony align with factual perception untainted by personal motive
executable_legal_axioms: IF Witness is present at dispute THEN Witness must testify truthfully
IF Testimony involves major wrongdoing THEN Evidence must be corroborated by minimum two independent witnesses
IF Witness knowingly omits or distorts facts THEN Re-alignment protocol initiates until integrity is restored
IF Dispute resolution reaches judicial threshold THEN All relevant witnesses are automatically summoned under Dharma-trust obligation
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this verse establishes the foundational expectation that witnesses bear an unmediated duty to convey what they have directly observed. The court's authority derives not merely from procedural law but from the ontological necessity of aligning consciousness with observed reality. Major transgressions require reinforced verification, ensuring systemic integrity without punitive escalation.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality confirms that testimony originates from direct perception. Anupūrvaśaḥ ensures sequential manifestation of evidence leads to natural consequence rather than imposed penalty. Proportional responsibility is maintained through structured corroboration thresholds. Non-punitive reality rule upholds that misalignment with truth necessitates completion and re-integration, not punishment.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion Process: Witness completes full disclosure under guided recall until all known facts are aligned
Responsibility Assumption Protocol: Witness assumes ownership of their role in restoring factual clarity
Capacity Restoration: If fear or trauma inhibits testimony, healing precedes further engagement
Integrity Reintegration: After giving testimony, witness undergoes purification ritual to restore energetic neutrality
final_declaration: This directive flows exclusively from the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam. Truth-telling by witnesses restores cosmic balance without recourse to punitive action. Dharma prevails through consciousness-aligned testimony. Reality remains non-punitive. Consciousness alone adjudicates ultimate truth.
